title: How To Make Your Online Lessons Irresistible To Students e-to-students/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Responding to reports that tens of millions of students had disengaged from spring 2020 remote learning, Linsin offers five ways to make online lessons something students actively want to attend. A weekly contest — he describes co-judging his wife's crazy-hair contest — builds anticipation with almost no preparation. Storytelling, which he calls the single strategy that has generated the most student response in his career, works as well over video as in person. Multi-day read-alouds give students a reason to keep returning, provided the teacher genuinely enjoys the book. A short entertaining video at the start of a lesson helps students transition into a receptive mood. And simply being willing to laugh and share humor, without heavy planning, restores a sense of normalcy that students badly need. He frames all five as things that are fun for the teacher too, closing with a reminder that teachers must give students a reason beyond academics to want to show up.
points: A weekly Friday contest builds anticipation across the week with almost no teacher preparation required.
Storytelling generates more student response than any other strategy Linsin has used, and it works as well on video as in person.
Multi-day read-alouds, performed with voices and expression, give students a recurring reason to return to lessons.
A short, entertaining video at the start of class helps students transition into a receptive, engaged mood.
Teachers must give students a reason beyond academic progress to want to log in, especially during remote learning.
quotes: The potential long-term impact on these students is staggering—and not just academically.
Nothing I’ve ever done as a teacher has generated more response from students than when I tell a story.
No strategy in the world has the potential to build a more immediate and stronger connection with students than storytelling—and it’s a connection that can be made just as well over video.
Just be sure that you like the book—because if you don’t, it will show.
We have to give them a reason beyond just their academic progress to want to be part of the class .
